text:
sam: FYI - saw a tenant hit unexpected tail latency during a burst test. root cause looks like admission allowed too many inflight small requests which starved larger batched jobs.

marta: Ugh. Is the admission layer counting inflight *requests* or inflight *gpu-time*? we currently use request slots which seems too coarse.

sam: request slots. cheap to implement but desserts=

cheng: we should measure "inflight GPU-ms" instead. e.g., estimate cost = max(estimated_tokens*per_token_ms, min_slot_ms). That lets small fanout not crowd out long-running batches.

devon: +1. Also need a fast fallback if cost estimates are wrong. Suggest admission score + leaky bucket: accept if tenant_budget >= cost or if burst_credit>0 and backlog small.

marta: can we avoid pushing complex billing logic into the operator? where does autoscaler fit vs admission controller? we want operator to react to sustained headroom, not microbursts.

devon: operator should only see aggregated intent signals (headroom shortfall, sustained queue length). Admission controller lives on serving side and enforces per-request policies. important boundary: operator not responsible for per-request accounting.

sam: agreed. So implement per-request accounting in runtime, expose metrics: tenant_inflight_gpu_ms, tenant_burst_credit, tenant_queue_len. operator consumes those.

cheng: rough admission pseudocode I prototyped:

```
function admit(req):
  cost = estimate_gpu_ms(req)
  if tenant.burst_credit >= cost and tenant.queue_len < QUEUE_THRESH:
    tenant.burst_credit -= cost
    accept()
  elif tenant.inflight_gpu_ms + cost <= tenant.reservation_gpu_ms:
    tenant.inflight_gpu_ms += cost
    accept()
  else:
    reject_or_queue()
```

cheng: we also cap min cost to avoid high-fanout tiny requests getting freebies: cost = max(cost, MIN_COST_MS).

marta: nice. A few edge cases: 1) estimate under/over-run if model truncates; 2) preemptible tenants that we should deprioritize; 3) cross-tenant noisy-neighbor during rolling upgrades.

devon: for (1) we account actual_gpu_ms on completion and refund or debit burst_credit accordingly (can be negative briefly). for (2) admission checks a tenant priority class. for (3) operator can trigger migration or scale when aggregate sustained refund shows underprovision.

sam: ops-bot: can we get a dashboard card that surfaces tenant_inflight_gpu_ms and burst_credit over 1m/5m/1h windows?

ops-bot: created dashboard request #INC-4513 with basic panels: tenant_inflight_gpu_ms, burst_credit, queue_len. link: https://console/redwood/d/INC-4513

marta: should we expose a stable admit API so we can A/B different admission heuristics? e.g., admit_v1 (slots), admit_v2 (gpu-ms) and traffic split.

devon: yes. Add admit_version label to metrics and a rollout flag in tenant config. Operator can flip per-tenant.

cheng: one more thought: we need a small safety net for controller-degraded mode: if operator is unreachable, runtime should still enforce sane defaults (hard caps + small burst allowance) so we don't silently DOS upstream.

sam: next steps: devon to open RFC PR for admission-api + metrics (include rollout plan and operator binding). cheng to prototype estimate function and refund logic. marta to spec dashboard panels and tenant config fields.

marta: timeline? can we try a canary on test-dedicated pool this week?

devon: aiming PR today, canary early next week. I'll post PR link.

devon: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/2345 - admits v2 + metrics. runs behind feature flag.

sam: nice. thanks all, will watch the dashboard when canary lands. :thumbsup:
